_doc: worktree-ownership.json — WHICH BRANCH MAY TOUCH WHICH PATH, and which deploy surface each branch may push.
Why this file exists (measured 2026-09-05, D-194): `main` and `web-home` forked on 2026-08-27 and by
2026-09-05 nine files had been edited on BOTH sides — five of them deploy scripts (Caddyfile 1,733 lines
apart, caddy-deploy.sh, web-deploy.sh, publish-official.sh, heartbeat-pump.mjs). Hard rule #4 ('only ONE
session deploys') existed only as a sentence people had to remember; on 2026-09-04 two sessions deployed
Caddy fifteen minutes apart and were saved by luck (byte-identical output), not by any mechanism.
How it is read: `scripts/check-worktree-ownership.mjs`. A path is allowed on a branch when it matches one
of that branch's `owns` globs, or one of the `shared` globs, or — for the `defaultOwner` only — when no
other branch owns it. A path that matches ANOTHER branch's `owns` is a violation, whatever else it matches.
`deploys` lists the surfaces a branch may push to the server; deploy scripts ask the gate with `--deploy`.
Glob rules: `**` crosses directories, `*` and `?` do not; a pattern with no `/` matches a file name in any
directory. Branch names are matched to a table entry by `branchAliases` (regex → entry) when not literal.
Changing this table is a DECISION about who owns a surface, not a way to make the gate green: write the
reason in DECISIONS.md. The self-test also refuses a table in which two branches claim the same literal
path, because an ambiguous table is a table nobody can be red against.

shared._note: Editable from every branch. Merges will still conflict textually here — that is the price of a shared notebook, not a hazard on the product path.
shared._why_check_html: console-deploy.sh (main) parse-checks console/index.html with it and web-deploy.sh (web-home) parse-checks the site with it. One file, two callers, both legitimate — so it is shared on purpose, and whoever edits it must run BOTH callers.

main._surface: the chain: fork + patches, console, faucet, node images, the gates, and the publication script

web-home._surface: the public site and the edge in front of it: Next.js export, the /chains/ directory page, Caddy

audit._surface: read-only review; its core is pinned to one SHA and it never deploys (see its own CLAUDE.md)

_contested_2026-09-05._note: Files both branches had edited when this table was written. The owner named here wins; the other side's future edits go red. Moving the web-owned deploy files into local-net/deploy/web/ is the web session's job after it merges main (a rename on main would collide with 1,733 lines of Caddyfile changes on web-home).
_contested_2026-09-05.local-net/deploy/Caddyfile: web-home — the running Caddyfile comes from that branch (hard rule #4)
_contested_2026-09-05.local-net/deploy/publish-official.sh: main — publication is a main-side act; web-home receives it by merge
_contested_2026-09-05.local-net/faucet/heartbeat-pump.mjs: main — the pump's source lives in faucet/ and the ceremony runbook on main drives it
